what: Euryale the Gorgon, the far-roaming, immortal sister of Medusa, the wailer who still grieves for her beheaded sister: a tall, terrible winged woman-shaped monster standing on two legs, nothing like a living lady, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, with two arms only and no more. Her skin is cold ash-grey, the plain neutral grey of a weathered stone statue, on her face, neck and upper arms alike, a colour no living woman has. Her face is the gorgon mask from an old Greek shield, broad and monstrous, with a heavy brow, a flat wide nose, two huge round eyes filled to the brim with solid yellow light, and a very wide mouth stretched open from cheek to cheek in a howl, showing a row of teeth and two long white tusks curving up from the lower jaw. She has no hair at all. Out of her bare scalp grow five huge living snakes, each as thick as her forearm and as long as her arm, striped all along their length in broad bold rings of pale ivory-white and jet black, so each snake is plainly a snake even from far away. The five snakes fan out from her head in every direction like the rays of a crown, one straight up, two out to the left, two out to the right, each one rearing with its own head clear of the others against the backdrop, each snake's head wedge-shaped with its jaws gaping wide and two white fangs, its forked tongue flicking. The snakes are the biggest and brightest thing about her head. Her hands and forearms, from the elbow down, are solid bright bronze metal, polished and gleaming like a new bronze cauldron, plainly metal and never skin, and each bronze finger ends in a long hooked bronze claw. From her back grow two great wings of feathers of dull dark old gold, the dun brown-gold of tarnished brass, darker brown at the tips, never bright.
colours: cold ash-grey skin, huge solid glowing yellow eyes, white tusks, five huge snakes striped in bold rings of pale ivory-white and jet black, bright polished bronze hands and forearms with bronze claws, two great wings of dull dark old gold feathers, dun brown-gold like tarnished brass, a long mourning peplos of dark brown, the brown of a chestnut, with a broad black border, a narrow black wool shawl.
wears: She wears a long archaic Greek peplos of dark chestnut-brown wool with a broad black border at the hem, that covers her from the shoulders to the ankles; its skirt is heavy, thick, opaque wool, whole and closed all the way round from the waist to the ankles, a single unbroken bell of cloth that hides both legs completely; a narrow black wool mourning shawl lies over her shoulders and hangs down her back, well below her head, never over her head. No armour, no crown, no diadem, no jewels.
holds: Her hands are empty and she holds nothing: her left bronze hand is thrust forward with the claws spread, her right bronze hand is swept back behind her, open and empty, nowhere near her head.
pose: On two legs under the peplos, seen from the side and a little from the front, she rushes forward to the left in a long stalking stride, her body leaning far forward, her weight on her bent front leg, the skirt swinging, her face turned toward the viewer, her tusked mouth wide open in a long wailing howl, her left bronze arm thrust far forward at the viewer with the claws spread, her right bronze arm swept back behind her, the ringed snakes rearing out from her head in a wide fan with their jaws open, both golden wings raised high behind her and bent sharply at the wrist like two tall arches, tips pointing down.
must_show: a winged gorgon: a grey-skinned monster with a broad mask of a face, glowing yellow eyes and white tusks
five huge snakes ringed ivory-white and black fanning out from her head, readable as snakes in the small sprite
mouth wide open, wailing
hands and forearms of bright bronze metal with claws, both empty and flung wide
two great dark gold feathered wings
a long dark chestnut-brown peplos with a black border, fully clothed, no armour
different from Stheno: brown dress, ringed pale snakes, arms wide, not the black-snaked armoured fighter
must_not_show: snake tail for a lower body

what: a bronze sentinel, a copy of Talos, the giant of bronze that the smith-god Hephaestus made to guard Crete: a giant bronze statue of a Greek hoplite warrior come to life, cast in metal and nothing else, tall and broad-shouldered, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms and two legs. Every part of him is cast metal: bright brassy gold-bronze like a polished temple bell, with hard white glints of reflected light on every curve and edge and dark brown-black shadows in every crease and seam, so he plainly shines like metal and never looks like skin. His head is a cast bronze Corinthian helmet with a tall bronze crest, joined to him like part of the statue, its eye-slits dark, two small red-hot sparks of orange light glowing inside them. His chest is a bronze cuirass cast with the shapes of chest muscles, his shins are bronze greaves, and his bare arms and thighs are bronze too, all one metal. Both his hands and forearms glow red-hot, bright orange-red like iron fresh from the forge, the dark knuckles showing in the middle of the glow; the rest of him is gold-bronze.
colours: bright brassy gold-bronze metal over his whole body, helmet and crest, hard white glints, dark brown-black shadows in the seams, two small orange sparks in the helmet's eye-slits, red-hot glowing orange-red hands and forearms, one rough grey granite boulder.
wears: All of his gear is cast bronze and part of the statue: the crested Corinthian helmet, the cuirass, a short kilt of hanging bronze strips to mid-thigh, and the greaves. No cloth, no cloak, no shield.
holds: Both his hands together hold exactly one huge rough boulder of plain grey granite, as big as his own chest, lifted high above his helmet, his red-hot fingers spread on its underside. Nothing else is in his hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, he strides forward to the left with his weight on his bent front leg and his back leg stretched out behind, his body arched back as both arms heave the boulder high over his head, about to hurl it forward, his helmeted face turned toward the viewer.
must_show: a giant made entirely of shining gold-bronze metal, plainly a metal statue and not skin, head to feet
a bronze Corinthian helmet with a crest, bronze cuirass and greaves: a hoplite statue
a grey boulder lifted overhead in both hands, about to be hurled
red-hot glowing hands and forearms
a striding throwing pose

what: a handmaid of Hel, the Norse goddess of the dead, one of the slow-walkers who serve in her hall, painted seriously like a figure from a Norse saga, uncanny and menacing: a dead woman who walks again, half dead-dark like her mistress Hel. She is tall and thin, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms, but bent almost double with a hunched back, her head thrust forward and low. Her face is a corpse's face: cold dead skin of grey-blue like a drowned woman, deep hollow cheeks, a thin pinched nose, ears, heavy brows, thin blue-grey lips drawn back from long yellow teeth in a snarl, and two eyes that glow pale icy white with no pupils, staring up at the viewer from under her brows. Both her arms, from the shoulders down to the long fingers, are blackened rotting dead flesh, very dark slate-grey mottled with black, the skin shrunk tight over the bones so every knuckle and tendon shows, plainly bare dead flesh, never gloves; her fingers are long and bony, ending in long broken black nails like claws. Her bare feet are blackened the same way. Long straight lank grey-white hair hangs forward round her face in heavy strands.
colours: grey-blue dead skin on the face and neck, glowing pale icy white eyes, long yellow teeth, rotting blackened very dark slate-grey arms, hands and feet mottled with black, long lank grey-white hair, a long dress of very dark charcoal-grey wool, an apron-dress of dull rust-brown wool, two big oval bronze brooches, a big ladle of dark old wood.
wears: She wears the dress of a Norse woman: a long dress of very dark charcoal-grey wool covering her from the neck to the ankles, its sleeves torn off at the shoulder so her blackened arms are bare, and over it a long apron-dress of dull rust-brown wool hung from two shoulder straps, ragged at the hem; where each strap meets the apron, high on her chest, is pinned one big oval brooch of dull bronze, domed like a turtle shell. No crown, no hood, no armour.
holds: In her right hand, raised high over her head like a club, she holds exactly one big wooden ladle: one straight thick handle of dark old wood as long as her arm, with one deep round wooden cup at its upper end, the cup as big as her head. Her left hand is empty: a blackened bony clawed hand thrust out toward the viewer at the level of her face, fingers spread and hooked to seize. Nothing else is in her hands. She has no staff.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, she shuffles forward to the left, bent almost double, slow but menacing, her weight on her bent front leg, her back foot dragging, her head low and thrust forward, glaring up at the viewer with glowing white eyes and bared teeth, her blackened left claw reaching out to seize, the big ladle raised high in her right hand ready to swing down, her lank hair hanging forward.
must_show: a hunched, stooped dead woman with a grey-blue corpse face, glowing white eyes and bared teeth: plainly dead and plainly menacing
rotting blackened bare arms and clawed hands, plainly flesh, not gloves
a dark Norse dress with a rust-brown apron-dress and oval bronze brooches, fully clothed
one big wooden ladle raised high in the right hand like a weapon
the blackened left claw empty, reaching to seize
a slow, bent, shuffling but threatening pose
must_not_show: a cloud of mist round her

what: a mere-wife, one of the kind of Grendel's mother from the Old English poem Beowulf: a monstrous she-troll, a water-hag who lives under the black water of a mere, painted seriously and frighteningly, never pretty, never a mermaid. She is plainly female and plainly a monster: taller than a man, with a woman's shape but a troll's size, long-bodied with a long neck, broad bony shoulders, long powerful arms reaching to her knees with huge long-fingered hands, long legs, and a long ragged dress that flares out to her ankles like a skirt. Her skin is wet, slimy and glistening, very dark murky grey-green, the dull colour of a pike's back, mottled with black blotches and rough with small scales on the shoulders and forearms, a colour no living person has, on her face, neck, arms, hands and feet alike. Her face is a troll's face, never a woman's: a long heavy face with a long hooked nose, a heavy brow, long pointed ears sticking out through her hair, a jutting underbite jaw with two big yellow tusks rising from the lower jaw over her upper lip, a wide mouth full of jagged yellow fangs, and two small round eyes glowing pale lamp-yellow. Her hair is very long, lank and soaking wet, jet black, hanging from her head down past her waist in heavy dripping strands that swing as she moves. Her fingers end in long hooked black claws, her feet are long and webbed with black claws.
colours: wet slimy very dark murky grey-green skin, the dull colour of a pike's back, mottled with black, glowing pale lamp-yellow eyes, yellow tusks and fangs, very long lank wet jet-black hair, a long ragged dress of very dark brown hide, the colour of wet peat, a belt of knotted dark rope, a short broad knife with a dark iron blade and a dark wooden grip, black claws.
wears: She wears a long ragged dress of very dark brown untanned hide, the colour of wet peat, that covers her from the neck to the ankles, close at the chest and waist and flaring out into a long torn skirt below a knotted dark rope belt, its hem in dripping tatters round her ankles. Her arms are bare from the shoulder. No armour, no jewels.
holds: In her right hand she holds exactly one broad seax: a heavy single-edged knife as long as her forearm, perfectly straight, as broad as her palm, a dark iron blade with a dark wooden grip, held low at her hip, point forward. Her left hand is empty: a huge dark clawed hand stretched forward toward the viewer at the height of her face, long fingers spread, reaching to grab and drag. Nothing else is in her hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, she lunges forward to the left out of the dark, body pitched forward and stooped, her weight on her bent front leg, her back leg stretched out behind under the flaring skirt, her empty clawed left hand reaching far ahead at the viewer to grab, the seax held low at her right hip ready to stab, her fanged mouth open in a snarl, her long wet black hair swinging forward.
must_show: a monstrous she-troll, plainly female: long flaring ragged dress, very long lank wet black hair past the waist
plainly a monster, not a woman: wet dark grey-green scaly skin, a long hooked nose, pointed ears, tusks, glowing yellow eyes
one straight broad seax in the right hand
the left clawed hand empty, reaching to grab
legs and clawed feet under the skirt: not a mermaid

what: a galla, one of the demons of the Sumerian underworld who dragged Inanna's husband Dumuzi down to the land of no return, painted like a creature from an old Mesopotamian stone relief brought to life: a lean, wiry, fully fleshed demon with realistic adult proportions, long limbs, two arms, standing on two legs. Its skin is dull grey-brown, the colour of dried river mud, on its arms, chest and legs alike, a colour no living person has. It has the whole head of a lion on a man's neck, a big head: a broad flat lion's face with a big shaggy mane of very dark brown hair, nearly black, framing the whole face like a ruff and falling over its shoulders, wide-open lion jaws baring four huge white fangs, a wrinkled snarling muzzle, and two round staring eyes glowing pale yellow. Its legs end below the knee in the scaly legs of a great bird of prey, dark grey, with three long toes in front, each ending in a long hooked black talon. Its hands end in long hooked black claws.
colours: dull grey-brown skin like dried river mud, a lion's face with a big shaggy very dark brown mane, pale yellow glowing eyes, white fangs, dark grey scaly bird's legs with black talons, a knee-length kilt of shaggy dark brown goat-hair fleece, a broad black leather belt, a club of dark wood.
wears: It wears a Sumerian kilt from the waist to the knee, made of shaggy dark brown goat-hair fleece hanging in long ragged tufts, held up by a broad black leather belt. Its chest, arms and bird's legs are bare. No armour, no helmet, no jewels.
holds: In its right hand, raised high over its head, it holds exactly one club: one straight thick length of dark wood as long as its arm, narrow at the grip, swelling to a heavy knobbly end, nothing fixed to it. Its left hand is empty: a grey-brown clawed hand thrust far forward at the viewer, fingers spread and hooked to seize. Nothing else is in its hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, it rushes forward to the left with its weight on its bent front leg and its back leg stretched out behind, body pitched forward, its left claw reaching out ahead to grab, its right arm raised high swinging the club, its lion's head turned to the viewer with its jaws wide open in a roar.

dark scaly bird-of-prey legs with talons
a shaggy dark brown fleece Sumerian kilt

what: an ushabti worker, one of the little servant figures of glazed faience that were buried in Egyptian tombs to do the dead man's work in the fields, risen up man-sized and alive and hard at work: a tomb figurine of glazed pottery that moves, not a mummy and not a living man, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, about eight heads tall, two arms. Its whole body is one glossy glazed surface of deep Egyptian faience blue, a dark rich blue like old glazed tomb pottery, darker in every hollow, with pale shine on the curves and fine black crazing cracks in the glaze; never bright cyan. It is shaped like a mummy case, as real ushabtis are: its two legs are pressed together inside one smooth tight glazed sheath from the hips down to the ankles, so from the waist down it is one tapering column with no knees and no gap between the legs, ending in two small feet that shuffle together. Across the front of that column run five broad horizontal bands of bold black painted hieroglyph signs, like writing on a pot, the biggest marks on its body. It bends at the waist like a man working a field. Its head is glazed the same deep blue: the calm blank face of a man with big black painted almond eyes and black painted eyebrows, a straight nose, closed lips. On its head is a plain wig painted solid glossy black that falls in two broad flaps to the chest.
colours: deep glossy Egyptian faience blue glaze on the whole body, head and arms, darker in the hollows, five broad bands of black painted hieroglyphs across the column of its legs, black painted eyes and eyebrows, a solid glossy black painted wig, a hoe with a dark wooden handle and a dull bronze blade, a woven basket of pale straw slung on its back.
wears: It wears nothing but its glaze: the black wig and the black hieroglyphs are painted on. A small round woven basket of pale straw hangs on its back from a cord over one shoulder, the way the baskets are painted on real ushabtis. No collar, no kilt, no headcloth, no bandages.
holds: Both its hands grip exactly one Egyptian hoe: one short thick handle of dark wood with one long broad blade of dull brown bronze fixed across its end, curving down like a bird's beak, sticking out to one side only. Nothing else is in its hands.
pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front, the column-bodied figure is bent far forward at the waist like a field-labourer, its back nearly level, its sheathed legs straight and together like a post leaning forward, both arms swinging the hoe down in a hard chopping stroke in front of it toward the left, the hoe's bronze blade at the bottom of the swing, the basket bouncing on its back, its calm painted face turned to the viewer: a little tomb statue come alive and hard at work.
must_show: a man-sized glossy deep-blue faience figurine, plainly glazed pottery, not a mummy and not a blue man
a mummy-case column from the waist down, legs together in one sheath, with bold black hieroglyph bands
a plain solid black painted wig
one bronze hoe swung down hard with both hands: a working pose, bent at the waist

what: an ushabti overseer, the foreman figurine buried with every ten Egyptian tomb workers to keep them at their labour, grown to the size of a man and come alive: a man-sized figurine of glazed pottery, not a mummy and not a living man, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms and two legs. Like a real overseer figurine it is made in the dress of the living and strides on two separate legs. Its whole body is one glossy glazed surface of deep Egyptian faience blue, a dark rich blue-green like old glazed tomb pottery, darker deep blue-black in every hollow and shadow, with a few small pale highlights on the curves and fine black crazing cracks; never bright, never pale. Rows of small black painted hieroglyph signs run in bands round its arms and legs. Its head is a carved figurine's head glazed the same deep blue: a stern face with big black painted almond eyes and heavy black painted eyebrows, a straight nose, a hard set mouth, and a short false beard of black glaze on its chin.
colours: deep glossy Egyptian faience blue glaze, a dark rich blue-green, deep blue-black in the shadows, on the whole body, head, arms and legs, black painted hieroglyph bands, black painted eyes and eyebrows, a pharaoh's headcloth striped in broad bands of black and bright gold-yellow, a stiff triangular kilt of bright gold-yellow glaze, a broad painted collar of black and gold-yellow bands, a whip with a black handle and three thick black lashes.
wears: On its head it wears a pharaoh-style striped headcloth that covers the top of the head and falls in two flaps to the chest, striped in broad bands of black and bright gold-yellow. It wears a stiff triangular kilt of bright gold-yellow glaze that juts forward in a point, and a broad painted collar of black and gold-yellow bands across its chest. All of it is glaze and paint on the figure. No bandages.
holds: In its right hand, raised high over its head, it holds exactly one overseer's whip: a short thick black handle with three thick black lashes, each as thick as a finger, swinging out in a curve against the backdrop. Its left arm is thrust straight out ahead of it, the left hand pointing commandingly with one finger at the viewer, nothing in it. Nothing else is in its hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, it strides forward to the left with its left foot far in front like an Egyptian statue walking, its body upright and stiff, its right arm raised high cracking the whip, its left arm pointing straight out in command, its stern painted face turned toward the viewer.

a black-and-gold striped headcloth and a short black false beard
a gold-yellow triangular kilt and a black-and-gold collar: dressed as the living, striding on two legs
black hieroglyph bands painted on the body
